items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Chonnonton peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.
Mayor McCabe offered additional reflections on the effects of colonialism on Indigenous people.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with moments of reflection:
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: The International Day of Persons with Disabilities is a day for celebration
notes: and reflection.

In our own community, we celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Grand River Accessibility Committee (GRAAC). Members of GRAAC have enriched our community by identifying and overseeing the removal of barriers for people with disabilities in Waterloo and across the Region.
Their commitment to inclusion benefits us all, whether we are disabled or temporarily able-bodied.

Beyond GRAAC, disabled people continue to advocate and educate. A lot has been accomplished, but there is still so much to do. Today, we reflect on the impact of ableism and the many barriers that continue to keep disabled people from participating fully at work, school, play and in civic life.
Today, we re-commit ourselves to the long-term work of creating an inclusive and accessible community where everyone can participate, contribute, belong and thrive.

items.title: On Friday, we will remember the 14 women who were killed at l’École
notes: Polytechnique in Montreal 35 years ago and all those who have lost their lives to gender-based violence.

This solemn anniversary is a time to reflect on the harmful effects of patriarchy that put women, girls, two spirit and gender-diverse people at disproportionate risk of violence simply because of their gender. We are reminded that other aspects of identity further increase this risk. The crisis of missing and murdered Indigenous women, girls, Two Spirit and gender- diverse people has made this clear. As do increased incidents of violence against young women, trans people and women with disabilities.
As a City, we re-commit ourselves stopping gender-based violence in all its forms, and to creating communities that are safe for women, girls, two- spirit, trans and gender diverse people.

Michelle Lee gave a presentation outlining the current timeline for 2025 University Avenue East, the requirements for the expressions of interest, and the preferred proponent for the site. items.title: Official Plan Amendment 58: Official
notes: Plan Review (Phase 1)
Report No.: IPPW2024-061
Prepared By: Ric Martins
Ward No.: City-Wide

Ric Martins gave a presentation outlining the proposed changes to the Official Plan, including highlights and what has changed since the June 2024 draft. He then explained the next steps for the review. Ric Martins and Adam Lauder responded to questions of Council.

Melissa Durrell, Spokesperson, Build Urban requested that the Official Plan be less prescriptive, that details such as height limits and density fall under the Zoning By-law, and asked that the Official Plan Review be deferred. She then responded to questions of Council.
Laura Jamieson, Intermediate Planner, Zelinka Priamo Ltd. requested flexibility in policies to permit residential development on a site-specific basis, where appropriate.
She then responded to questions of Council. Ric Martins also responded to questions of Council.

Ryan Mounsey, CEO, Urban Insights Inc. gave a presentation outlining the correspondence that Urban Insights submitted on behalf of their clients and offered some policy recommendations related to the Official Plan Review surrounding height and density, and parking reductions. He asked for certain properties to be deferred to work through the planning aspects of the development applications. He then responded to questions of Council. Adam Lauder also responded to questions of Council.

Trevor Hawkins, Partner, MHBC Planning spoke about the correspondence that MHBC submitted on behalf of Wilfrid Laurier University, and asked for Council to consider revisions to the amendments, specifically in regards to the structure being proposed around campus master planning, and to allow flexibility surrounding owning and operating housing on campus. He then responded to questions of Council. Adam Lauder responded to questions of Council.

Kevin Thomason, Vice-Chair, Grand River Environmental Network (GREN) spoke in support of the new Official Plan, specifically surrounding the positive environmental aspects of it. He then responded to questions of Council.

Kae Elgie, Resident of Waterloo gave a presentation thanking Council and staff for listening to citizens, working to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and intensifying in ways that respect community and farmland. She then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.
Adam Lauder responded to questions of Council.
